mainTopic: How strongly a טבול יום affects קדשים, why benefit stays forbidden after a bird חטאת's blood is sprinkled, and whether squeezing out its blood (מיצוי) is essential.
overview: The עמוד opens with a ברייתא giving three views on how strongly a טבול יום affects קודש. אבא שאול treats him as a ראשון. רבי מאיר says he makes קודש טמא. חכמים say he only makes it פסול. רבא explains that all three agree on the Torah law, so our משנה fits everyone. The stricter views are a rabbinic מעלה for קדשים, and for חכמים immersion has weakened his טומאה. Next, the גמרא asks why benefit from a bird חטאת is still forbidden after its blood is sprinkled. רבי חנינא answers that the משנה speaks of meat that went out of its area, following רבי עקיבא. Then רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה report רב differently on whether squeezing out the blood (מיצוי) is essential. A פסוק is used to challenge רב הונא, and he reads it as 'only if blood is left.' Finally, רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges that reading from the leftover of a מנחה, a point that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of אבא שאול's view and the view of רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes אבא שאול's opinion that a טבול יום is a first-degree impurity for קודש. It then gives רבי מאיר's view that he makes קודש טמא and makes תרומה פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: [אבא שאול says a טבול יום is] a first-degree impurity for sacred food. רבי מאיר says: he makes sacred food impure, and he disqualifies תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a ברייתא about a טבול יום. It finishes אבא שאול's opinion and then brings רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול is the strictest: for קודש, the טבול יום acts like a ראשון לטומאה, so food he touches becomes a שני and can pass impurity further down the chain. רבי מאיר is one level softer: he makes קודש truly טמא, but for תרומה he only makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed in a מקוה today but is not fully pure until nightfall
A 'beginning' of impurity: first-degree (ראשון)
Sacred food, such as sacrificial meat
Makes impure, so the item can pass impurity onward
Disqualifies: the item becomes unfit but does not pass impurity onward

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מטמא and פוסל. מטמא means the food becomes impure and can spread impurity. פוסל means the food just becomes unusable, and the chain stops there.

phrases.english: Is first-degree impure with regard to sacred food.
Rabbi Meir says:
He renders sacred food impure,
And disqualifies תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול: a טבול יום is a ראשון for קודש. רבי מאיר: he makes קודש טמא and makes תרומה פסול.

steps.title: חכמים say a טבול יום only disqualifies, for both תרומה and קודש
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say a טבול יום treats קודש exactly like תרומה. He only disqualifies food and drink, and does not make them טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: just as he disqualifies תרומה drinks and תרומה foods, so too he disqualifies sacred drinks and sacred foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third and most lenient view. For חכמים, a טבול יום never makes anything truly impure, not even קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, there is no difference between תרומה and קודש here. In both, the food or drink becomes פסול and cannot pass impurity on. Our משנה also says the טבול יום only disqualifies, so at first glance the משנה matches only חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Drink or liquid
Foods
The portion of produce given to a כהן, holy but less holy than קודש

steps.whyThisMatters: This view lines up with our משנה. That raises the question the גמרא answers next: does our משנה reject אבא שאול and רבי מאיר?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Just as he disqualifies
תרומה liquids and תרומה foods,
So too he disqualifies
Sacred liquids and sacred foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion in the same ברייתא, the opposite end from אבא שאול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טבול יום only makes תרומה and קודש פסול. He never makes them טמא.

steps.title: רבא: אבא שאול is describing an extra rabbinic stringency for קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that אבא שאול's strict view is only a rabbinic מעלה (extra stringency) for קדשים. By Torah law he could agree with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: according to אבא שאול, the Rabbis made an extra stringency for sacred items, and they treated a טבול יום like a first-degree impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins showing that our משנה does not have to follow only חכמים. He starts by explaining that אבא שאול's view is a rabbinic add-on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is speaking about Torah law, where a טבול יום only disqualifies. אבא שאול's 'ראשון' status comes from a rabbinic מעלה for קדשים, so it does not clash with the משנה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra rabbinic stringency, usually to protect the holiness of קדשים
Sacred items or offerings
They made them equal to, or treated them like
First-degree impurity

steps.confusionAlert: אבא שאול is not saying the Torah makes a טבול יום a ראשון. רבא explains that this is a rabbinic stringency layered on top of the Torah law.

phrases.english: Rava said:
According to Abba Shaul,
They made a higher standard for sacred items,
The Rabbis equated
One who immersed that day to a first-degree impurity,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל מַעֲלָה עָשׂוּ בַּקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden problem raised by steps 1-2: our משנה seemed to fit only חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting Torah law from rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה, which says a טבול יום only disqualifies, argues with אבא שאול and follows only חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law even אבא שאול agrees a טבול יום only disqualifies. His stricter view is a rabbinic מעלה for קדשים.

steps.title: רבא: for רבי מאיר, the stringency is to treat him like a second-degree food
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the rabbinic stringency treats a טבול יום like a food that is a שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, [the Rabbis treated him] like a second-degree food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies the same answer to רבי מאיר. His view is also a rabbinic stringency, just one level lighter than אבא שאול's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שני can make קודש טמא as a שלישי but only makes תרומה פסול. That matches exactly what רבי מאיר said in step 1. So רבי מאיר is also adding a rabbinic layer and does not argue with the Torah law in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Food with second-degree impurity

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir,
Like a food of second-degree impurity.
phrases.notes: The words 'the Rabbis treated him' are carried over from the line before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer, now applied to רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting Torah law from rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר holds that by Torah law a טבול יום makes קודש טמא, which would contradict our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's 'מטמא את הקודש' is a rabbinic stringency that treats the טבול יום like an אוכל שני.

steps.title: For חכמים, immersion weakens his impurity, so he disqualifies but does not make impure
steps.stepSummary: חכמים add no stringency. Since he has already immersed, his טומאה is weakened: he can make things פסול but not טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the חכמים: since he immersed, the impurity is weakened. He makes things disqualified, but he does not make them impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes by explaining the reasoning of חכמים. This wraps up his answer that our משנה can fit all three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing in a מקוה already lowered his טומאה, so חכמים saw no reason to make him stricter for קדשים. That is why for them he only makes things פסול. Since everyone agrees on this as the Torah-level rule, our משנה fits all the views.

keyTerms.meaning: Became weak or diluted
Immersed
Makes into, or gives the status of
Disqualified, unfit but not passing on impurity
Impure

steps.whatToRemember: All three opinions agree that by Torah law a טבול יום only makes things פסול. אבא שאול (ראשון) and רבי מאיר (שני) add a rabbinic מעלה for קדשים. חכמים add nothing, because the immersion has already weakened his טומאה. So our משנה fits everyone.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, since he has immersed,
The impurity is weakened,
He renders it disqualified,
But he does not render it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's three-part explanation with the reasoning of חכמים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because immersion weakens his טומאה, a טבול יום only makes קודש פסול, not טמא. The stricter views are rabbinic stringencies, so our משנה fits every opinion.

steps.title: Why is benefit still forbidden after the blood is sprinkled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, infers that benefit is still forbidden after sprinkling, and challenges this: the meat now belongs to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that once the blood was sprinkled, one is liable for פיגול, נותר and טמא, but not for מעילה. That means there is no מעילה, but there is still a prohibition. Why? The meat is now the כהנים' property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and reads into its wording that benefit is still forbidden. Then it asks why that should be so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says there is no מעילה, which suggests a lighter איסור still remains. But once the blood is sprinkled, the כהנים are allowed to eat a חטאת. So something they may eat should not be forbidden at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש property; it brings a קרבן and payment
A prohibition, here a lighter one than מעילה
The property of the כהנים
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Once its blood was sprinkled, one is liable, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה about a bird חטאת. The 'etc.' stands for liability for פיגול, נותר and טמא, but not מעילה.

phrases.english: It is only misuse that does not apply,
but a prohibition does apply.
But why?
It is the property of the priests!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It returns to an earlier line of the משנה about a bird חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that an איסור of benefit remains after sprinkling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After sprinkling, the meat belongs to the כהנים and they may eat it, so no איסור should remain.

steps.title: The משנה is speaking about meat taken out, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that the משנה speaks about meat that left its permitted area. According to רבי עקיבא, sprinkling still removes מעילה from such meat, but it may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: the משנה is talking about meat that went out of its area. This follows רבי עקיבא, who said that sprinkling works for meat that went out, so there is no מעילה, even though it is not fit to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question by narrowing the case of the משנה to meat that was taken out of the place where it may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that left the עזרה is פסול for eating, so it never becomes food the כהנים may eat. According to רבי עקיבא, the sprinkling still frees it from מעילה. That is why the משנה says no מעילה applies, yet an איסור remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat taken out of the area where it may be eaten
Throwing or sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Here: it works, meaning it removes the מעילה status
Fit to be eaten

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: It refers to those that went out,
phrases.notes: He means meat that left the area where it is allowed to be eaten.

phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Akiva,
who said that sprinkling is effective for that which went out,
phrases.notes: 'Effective' here means the sprinkling takes away the מעילה.

phrases.english: even though it is not fit for eating.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה (אוקימתא) according to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה speaks about normal meat that the כהנים may eat
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about meat that went out. Sprinkling removes מעילה, but eating it is still forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, זריקה removes מעילה even from meat that went out, but that meat stays forbidden to eat. This explains 'no מעילה, but still an איסור.'

steps.title: רב הונא: squeezing out the blood is not essential
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב that failing to squeeze out the blood of a bird חטאת does not invalidate it, because רב's version of the משנה reads 'its blood was sprinkled.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: squeezing out the blood of a bird חטאת is not essential, since רב's version of the משנה says 'its blood was sprinkled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the bird חטאת. Squeezing out the blood after sprinkling is not required for the קרבן to be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's version of the משנה ties the change in status to the sprinkling alone. So once the blood is sprinkled the קרבן is complete, and the squeezing that follows is only an extra step.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressing the bird's neck against the מזבח so the rest of the blood drains out
A bird sin offering
Essential; without it the קרבן is not valid
Its blood was sprinkled

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Squeezing out the blood of a bird sin offering is not essential.
For Rav teaches in the mishna: 'Its blood was sprinkled.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: מִיצּוּי חַטַּאת הָעוֹף אֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the words 'הוזה דמה' quoted in step 6 and raises a new question about them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיצוי of a bird חטאת is not essential

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: squeezing out the blood is essential
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה reports רב the opposite way: squeezing out the blood is essential, because רב's version of the משנה reads 'its blood was squeezed out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: squeezing out the blood of a bird חטאת is essential, and רב's version of the משנה says 'its blood was squeezed out.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second student reports רב's view the opposite way, based on a different wording of the same line in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the משנה ties the change in status to the squeezing, not to the sprinkling. That shows the קרבן is not complete until the blood is squeezed out. So the whole argument depends on which wording רב taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Its blood was squeezed out

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions are said in the name of the same רב. They are not arguing with רב. They disagree about what רב taught, and each one shows it from the wording of the משנה he had.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether מיצוי is essential depends on the wording of the משנה. 'הוזה דמה' means it is not essential, and 'מיצה דמה' means it is essential.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
Squeezing out the blood of a bird sin offering is essential.
And Rav teaches in the mishna: 'Its blood was squeezed out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב: מִיצּוּי חַטַּאת הָעוֹף מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite report of רב's view from step 8, based on a different wording of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיצוי of a bird חטאת is essential

steps.title: The verse seems to support רב אדא בר אהבה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the leftover blood must be squeezed out and then calls it a חטאת. That fits רב אדא בר אהבה, but what would רב הונא do with the word 'והנשאר'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out at the base of the altar; it is a sin offering.' This fits רב אדא בר אהבה well. But according to רב הונא, what does 'the remainder' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to make squeezing out the blood a required part of the חטאת, which is a problem for רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links squeezing out the blood (מיצוי) with the words 'it is a חטאת,' which suggests the offering only counts once the blood is squeezed out. That matches רב אדא בר אהבה's version of רב. רב הונא said squeezing is not essential, so the גמרא asks how he reads 'the remainder.'

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (according to one view)
shall be squeezed out (the blood is pressed out of the bird)
the base of the altar
and the remainder (the blood that is left over)

phrases.english: Come and hear: "And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out
at the base of the altar; it is a sin offering."
Granted, according to Rav Adda bar Ahava,
this is what is written:
"And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out... it is a sin offering,"
But according to Rav Huna, what is the meaning of "the remainder"?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״וְהַנִּשְׁאָר בַּדָּם יִמָּצֵה אֶל יְסוֹד הַמִּזְבֵּחַ חַטָּאת הִיא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a פסוק to test the two reports of רב's opinion from steps 8 and 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that failing to squeeze out the blood does not invalidate the bird חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק joins the squeezing to 'it is a חטאת,' which implies that squeezing is essential.

steps.title: רב הונא reads the verse as 'if blood is left over'
steps.stepSummary: 'והנשאר' means only that if some blood happens to be left, it should be squeezed out. 'חטאת היא' goes back to the sprinkling at the start of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'if some remained.' And what does 'it is a sin offering' refer to? To the first part of the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the פסוק so that squeezing becomes a conditional, non-essential step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no duty to make sure blood is left for squeezing; you squeeze only if some happens to remain. The words 'it is a חטאת,' which seemed to make squeezing essential, are moved back to the sprinkling on the side of the altar. Only the sprinkling is what makes the offering valid.

keyTerms.meaning: that if (some) remained, so it is conditional, not required
on the first part (of the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, only the sprinkling is essential. Squeezing out the blood happens only if blood is left over, and 'חטאת היא' refers back to the sprinkling.

phrases.english: As it was taught by the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
that if some remained.
phrases.notes: So you squeeze only if blood happens to be left. You don't have to make sure some is left.

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of "it is a sin offering"?
It refers to the first part.
phrases.notes: The first part of the פסוק is the sprinkling of blood on the side of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 on behalf of רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: a word is read as conditional, and a phrase is moved to an earlier clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'והנשאר... חטאת היא' makes squeezing essential to the חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והנשאר' means 'if some is left.' 'חטאת היא' refers to the sprinkling, so squeezing is not essential.

steps.title: Does 'what is left' of a מנחה also mean 'only if some is left'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the 'if some remained' reading. The same kind of word, 'והנותרת,' is used for a מנחה. Would that also mean nothing has to be left over for the כהנים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: If so, regarding a מנחה, where it is written 'and what is left,' should that also mean 'if some is left'? And if you say: yes, that is indeed so,
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge attacks the 'if some remained' reading by applying it to a מנחה. The גמרא is setting up a further point that continues past this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'leftover' language always means 'only if something happens to be left,' then the leftover of a מנחה would not have to be kept for the כהנים either. The challenger expects someone might accept this ('הכי נמי'), and he is about to show why that cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now… (a challenge that pushes a reading to an unwanted result)
a meal offering made of flour
and what is left over (of the מנחה, given to the כהנים)
And if you say: yes, indeed so (an answer the challenger expects and is about to refute)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
But if so, regarding a meal offering,
where it is written: "And what is left over"
does it also mean "if some was left over"?
And if you would say: yes, that is indeed so,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading 'שאם נשאר' used in step 11 by applying it to a parallel word about the מנחה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'leftover' language as merely conditional ('if some remained').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the same reading to 'והנותרת' of a מנחה would mean nothing needs to be left for the כהנים. That seems unacceptable, and the refutation continues on the next עמוד.
